note: rc.6 republishes the Playground engine fix (bf4e2bd6) that no published version carries: a @zeus-js/web-c export could not mount the element it had just defined, so every WebC export in the Playground preview was blank. The published 0.2.0-rc.5 tarball contains 0 occurrences of the fixed guard and 1 of the broken one, which is why the Playground browser gate could not pass against it. rc.6 also carries the wasm build wiring (25d3cfda, bcc3d49b, 576b39a5) that the browser compiler needs on every publishing path. firstPublish is empty: all 32 fixed packages have been published before, so npm will not re-bind the latest tag for any of them. This is the first rc of the 0.2.0 line that is a genuine pair rather than a bootstrap or recovery: rc.5 published successfully, so neither exception applies and a real UI commit is required. check:release-pairing requires the pair to be one version, so the UI workspace moved from its 0.1.0-beta.35 line onto 0.2.0-rc.6 for this pair; the separate beta line is retired for the duration of the RC. The UI commit was cut before rc.6 published, so its lockfile does not yet resolve — check:ui-pairing verifies the pins, not the lockfile, and the lockfile is regenerated once rc.6 is on the registry.
